definition: Sentence boundary disambiguation (SBD), also known as sentence breaking, sentence boundary detection, and sentence segmentation, is the problem in natural language processing of deciding where sentences begin and end.
details: Natural language processing tools often require their input to be divided into sentences; however, sentence boundary identification can be challenging due to the potential ambiguity of punctuation marks. In written English, a period may indicate the end of a sentence, or may denote an abbreviation, a decimal point, an ellipsis, or an email address, among other possibilities. About 47% of the periods in The Wall Street Journal corpus denote abbreviations. Question marks and exclamation marks can be similarly ambiguous due to use in emoticons, source code, and slang. Some languages including Japanese and Chinese have unambiguous sentence-ending markers.

explainer.lead: Sentence boundary disambiguation (SBD) is the NLP task of deciding where sentences start and end. It matters because most downstream tools assume sentence-segmented input, yet punctuation is often ambiguous.

tiers.eli5: Figuring out where one sentence stops and the next begins is tricky because a dot can mean the end of a sentence, an abbreviation, a decimal point, or part of an email address.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use SBD as a preprocessing step before tokenization, parsing, or translation. A common pitfall is over-relying on simple period-splitting rules, which break on abbreviations and decimals; rule-based or ML segmenters are preferred.
tiers.paperLevel: SBD identifies sentence boundaries in raw text; for English, a period may denote a sentence end, abbreviation, decimal, ellipsis, or email address, and about 47% of periods in the Wall Street Journal corpus denote abbreviations. Question and exclamation marks add further ambiguity, and there is no perfect universal rule.

explainer.example: In 'Dr. Smith arrived at 3.5 p.m. yesterday.', SBD must recognize that the period after 'Dr' and 'p.m' are abbreviations and that '3.5' is a decimal, so the whole string is one sentence.
